A chain now counts as in progress until its last step is over, so it can't show "Done" between steps. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

  - a step is waiting in its lane's queue;

content.content:
#### Chained Tasks

A prompt sent in Chain runs as steps, each saved in the history as a task of its own: first the Chain task itself, which writes the spec; then the same prompt sent to Code, told what the spec step did; and, when the chain asks for a post-build spec update, the same prompt sent to Spec once more, told what the code step did. Each step knows the one it was sent from, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. Only the steps the chain sends itself belong to it; a task sent to the other mode by hand, or resent, from one of its steps is a task of its own.
Each step runs in the lane of the work it does, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says: the Chain task and its spec follow-up in the spec lane, the code step in the code lane. A step is sent once the step before it finishes, never before, and takes its place in its lane's queue by when its chain was sent, not when the step itself was: behind every prompt waiting there that was sent before its chain, earlier chains' steps included, and ahead of every prompt sent after it. So a chain's code step never jumps ahead of a Code prompt, or another chain's code step, sent before the chain was, and a Code prompt sent while the chain's spec step ran waits for the chain's code step rather than coming between the chain's steps. Two steps whose chains were sent in the same order run in that order, whichever spec step finished first. Where nothing sent before its chain is waiting, it runs as soon as its lane is free, and straight away if it already is. Its place holds however it came to be queued, so a restart, with the queue read back from the project, keeps it there. The lane it leaves is free for its own queue meanwhile, so a Spec task sent while a chain's code step runs runs beside it. A step waiting for its lane shows in the queue like any prompt, and can be cancelled there, ending the chain. A step whose chain step before it failed or was cancelled is never sent.
Each step also runs where the work of its lane runs, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says: the spec steps in a container holding the spec and no code, the code step always on the host, with its protected locations. Each carries on its own lane's conversation, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, so a step is told what the step before it did only through its prompt: the Chain prompt as typed and that step's final output, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](./mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says.
In the previous tasks list, a chain's steps are grouped under one parent item, so they read as parts of a single chain. The parent is a heading row in the list, tinted the Chain colour, as the [PromptModesScope](./modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, a little more strongly than a single task's tint: a joined chain icon, the first line of the prompt, and at its right how many steps it has, "2 steps" or "3 steps". Its status is the chain's as a whole, never only that of its latest step: a chain is in progress from when it is sent until its last step is over, so it reads Running, with its spinner and its time counting, while any step is building, compiling, or running, while a step waits in its lane's queue, and while a step has finished Done and the chain has a step still to send, its code step, a spec follow-up it asks for, or a step added to it, between the one finishing and the next being sent. A step finishing Done never shows the chain as Done while another is still to come. Only once no step is under way, queued, or still to be sent is it over: Failed or Cancelled if a step was, and Done otherwise. While it is in progress, it is listed with the running tasks, in the Running group of the right sidebar's Tasks tab, with all its steps, done and to come, beneath it, never among the previous tasks, and it goes among them only once it is over. It has no checkbox, Resend, or Send to the other mode of its own, and clicking it doesn't open anything.
Beneath it, each step stays an item of its own, exactly as any previous task is, with its checkbox, status, Resend, and whatever else a task offers, opening onto its own prompt, table, and changed files. The steps are indented from the parent, joined to it by a thin line in the Chain colour down their left, from the parent's heading to the last step, and each is labelled by what it did, "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up", in that step's mode colour, before its prompt, which leaves out the prompt's first line when it is the parent's. They are listed in the order they ran.
A chain is listed where its first step was sent, oldest first like every other item; tasks sent while it ran, such as questions or tasks of the other lane run between its steps, are never listed within it, and are listed after the chain, in the order they were sent. A chain's steps are found by which step each was sent from, not by being next to each other in the history. A chain still running, or one whose later steps haven't been sent yet, shows as many steps as have been, and a step still running shows as it would anywhere. When the latest task, heading the view, is a step of a chain, that chain's earlier steps are still grouped under its parent in the list, the parent saying the rest is the latest task. A session divider never falls between a chain's steps: it goes above the chain's parent. A step from the history whose chain can't be worked out, as when the step it was sent from is missing, is listed as a task of its own.

#### Header
15:The right sidebar's Tasks tab: every task of the project at a glance, what has run, what is running, and what is queued, where any of them can be looked into, edited, and adjusted, and a chain given more steps.
26:Every task is one row, 28 pixels tall, as a queued prompt's is: a bar 2 pixels wide down its left edge in its mode's colour, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, then its status, a spinner while it is under way, a tick, cross, or dash once it has ended, or, queued, its place in the queue, then the first line of its prompt, cut off with an ellipsis, then, at its right, muted, how long it took, or has been running, as the [MessageList](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list) writes it. A chain is one row, its steps as rows indented beneath it, collapsed to start with, as the previous tasks group a chain. Clicking a row opens it, as below, and the row stays highlighted while it is open. Hovering a row shows its prompt's first lines in its tooltip.
30:The list is virtualized: however many tasks the project has run, it lays out and draws only the rows in view, and a few rows either side of it, never every row, so opening the tab, scrolling it, resizing the sidebar, filtering, and new tasks arriving cost the same with ten thousand previous tasks as with ten. Every row is 28 pixels tall, group headings and a chain's expanded steps included, so where each row lies is known from its place in the list alone, without laying out the rows before it, and the scrollbar's thumb is sized and placed from the whole list's height, as though every row were drawn.
31:A row is drawn only from what its row shows, its mode, status, first line, and time, read from each task's history record once and kept, never by reading a record's output, lines, or snapshots while scrolling; those are read only when a task is opened. Running rows update their time and spinner in place, redrawing only what is in view. Scrolling to a row, as when the tab opens on Running, a filter changes, or a queued row is dragged past the edge, jumps straight to its place without drawing the rows between. A row scrolled out of view and back is the same as it was, its chain expanded or not, its selection and highlight kept.
43:#### Chain Steps
45:An open Chain task lists its steps beneath its parameters, in the order they run, each a row as in the list, with its status: its spec step, its code step, and its spec follow-up when it has one. An "Add step" button beneath them adds a step of its own after the last: a Code or a Spec step, chosen from a small menu, with a prompt of its own, typed in the step's row as it expands, its model and effort those of the chain until changed. An added step runs once the step before it finishes, in its own mode's lane and place, as every step of a chain does, told its own prompt, the chain's prompt as typed, and what the step before it replied, as the spec-to-code prompt tells a code step, so a chain can be carried on, as a further code change once the spec is built, or a spec tidy-up after the code. A step not yet sent can be edited, moved among the others not yet sent, or removed; one sent reads as it was. Steps are saved with the chain, in its hidden anchor, as the [PromptSendingScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) keeps a queued prompt, so a chain keeps its added steps across restarts, and a step whose step before it failed or was cancelled is never sent, as none of a chain's are.

content.text:
A chain now reads Running until its last step is over, so it no longer shows "Done" between steps. The full test suite passes, including a new test that a chain between steps reads Running; I haven't watched it live in the app.

- **When it counts as running:** while any step is building, compiling or running, while a step waits in its lane's queue, or while a step finished Done and another is still to be sent (its code step, a spec follow-up, or an added step).
- **When it's over:** once nothing is running, queued or still to come, it reads Failed or Cancelled if a step was, and Done otherwise.
- **Time:** the chain's time keeps counting between steps.
- **Where it's listed:** while in progress, the chain sits in the Tasks tab's Running group as one row, with all its steps beneath it when expanded. It moves to Previous only once it's over, and the Previous count leaves out its steps until then.

The change is in `src/prompt_mode/tasks_tab.rs`, plus the chain status and time functions in `src/prompt_mode.rs`. This follows the spec, which matches your prompt.

One approximation: to tell that a queued prompt is the chain's own next step, I match on which step it was sent from and when the chain was sent. Chains don't keep that send time after a restart, so then a task you sent by hand from one of a chain's steps, if it's still queued, would also keep that chain showing Running.
